misconceptions.description: Assuming positive learner reactions prove instructional success
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats high satisfaction scores as sufficient evidence of impact
misconceptions.feedback: Reaction data is useful, but it is only one level of evidence. Strong evaluation also examines learning, behavior change, and organizational results.

misconceptions.description: Treating evaluation as something that happens only after launch
misconceptions.trigger: learner ignores formative evaluation during design and development
misconceptions.feedback: Evaluation should be continuous. Formative evaluation helps catch problems early, while summative evaluation judges final effectiveness later.

misconceptions.description: Confusing reaction, learning, behavior, and results data
misconceptions.trigger: learner labels quizzes as Level 1 or on-the-job performance as Level 2
misconceptions.feedback: The Kirkpatrick levels answer different questions. Reaction measures impressions, learning measures acquisition, behavior measures transfer, and results measures organizational outcomes.
